feedback.problem:
Let $V={R}^{3}$ be the vector space equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x,y⟩=5{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.
$$

If $x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]$ and 
$y=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $x$ and $y$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & =5{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =5\cdot (1\cdot 2)+3\cdot (4\cdot 0)+(-5)\cdot k \\  & =10+0-5k \\  & =10-5k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨x,y⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & =0 \\ 10-5k & =0 \\ 5k & =10 \\ k & =2\end{aligned}
$$
